description: Open ANY component from the registry by name as an interactive widget — use when the user wants to SEE or OPERATE the data (to merely read facts, use data_list — no UI). Works IMMEDIATELY for components saved moments ago in this same chat (the dedicated open_<name> tools may take a while to appear). Prefer reusing a component on a different collection over creating near-duplicate components.

collection.description: data collection to bind (default: the one the component declares, else its own name)

component.description: component name in the registry (see list_components)

name: open_component
title: Open any component

description: Internal: returns raw component HTML plus its trust tier and capability grants for the universal loader widget. Not useful to call directly — use get_component to read source.

offset.description: window the html (same grammar as get_component); omit for the whole document

name: component_html
title: Component HTML (internal)

description: READ THIS FIRST before creating or editing a component. Returns the window.oma API contract, available CSS design tokens, the data model, and a minimal working component template.

topic.description: which chapter (default basics: the contract + template). Each chapter stands alone

name: get_component_guide
title: Component authoring guide

description: List UI components in the registry (reusable across all chats). If the UI the user wants already exists, prefer opening it over creating a new one. Lists the user's openable apps by default — pass name to look one up, or widen with kind/visibility.

kind.description: default app: what a person opens and reuses

limit.description: cap the rows listed (the total is always reported)

name.description: exact component name — the fastest way to answer "open my X"

visibility.description: default featured+listed; archived/unlisted are retired or long-tail

name: list_components
title: List components

description: Read a component's HTML source as a WINDOW — offset/length select it, next_offset continues, total is the full length. Windows exist because some hosts silently drop the MIDDLE of an oversized result: a big component read whole can arrive mutilated with no sign, and an edit saved from it destroys the source. Carries version — the expected_version for edit_component / save_component.

length.description: max characters for this window (default fits the result budget)

name: get_component
title: Get component source

description: Create or update a UI component in the persistent registry. The HTML must follow the contract from get_component_guide (single self-contained HTML using window.oma; no external resources). After saving, open it IMMEDIATELY with open_component. Saving an existing name creates a new version (history kept).

description.description: one line: what this component shows and what data fields it uses

expected_version.description: REQUIRED when overwriting an existing component: the version you read (get_component). Creating a new name needs none

html.description: complete self-contained HTML document using window.oma

manifest.description: RETIRED — declare inside the html (see get_component_guide)

scene.description: RETIRED — declare inside the html (see get_component_guide)

name: save_component
title: Save component

description: Surgical edits to a component WITHOUT round-tripping the whole source: each edit replaces old_string (which must match exactly once, or set replace_all) with new_string. All edits apply together against expected_version, or nothing applies. No pre-read needed for source you just saved — your copy is byte-exact and your receipt carries the version; get_component is for source you did not write. The #oma-manifest block is re-read on save.

command_id.description: idempotency key — generate a fresh uuid per action

component.description: component name (this tool says `component`; save_component and get_component say `name`)

edits.description: applied in order; exact string match including whitespace

expected_version.description: REQUIRED — the version the edits were authored against (from get_component)

name: edit_component
title: Edit component source

description: Flip a component out of (or back into) the default listing. Archived apps stay fully intact — data, files, history, still openable by name — they just stop occupying the shelf. list_components {visibility: "archived"} shows them.

archived.description: true = archive; false = bring it back (listed)

command_id.description: idempotency key — generate a fresh uuid per action

name: archive_component
title: Archive / restore a component

description: Read items in full — every field, plus the item id you need to update or delete it. No UI (use open_component for that). Returns a PAGE: up to `limit` (default 100) matching items, with `total` and — when more exist — `next_cursor`; returned/total make a short delivery self-evident. `match` filters: a bare value means equals; an object is operators {ne, lt, lte, gt, gte, contains, prefix, exists} (numeric filters compare numerically, strings lexicographically — ISO dates work). Paging is a live keyset walk; items moved mid-page can be skipped or repeated.

cursor.description: opaque cursor from the previous page's next_cursor

match.description: filter on top-level fields, e.g. {"done": false} or {"amount": {"gte": 100}}

name: data_list

next_cursor.description: pass back as `cursor` for the next page; null = no more

total.description: how many items exist (the collection/group, pre-filter) — compare it with the rows you actually received

title: List collection data

description: Apply up to 200 writes in ONE transaction — for seeding an app from what you already know, or filling a board in one go, instead of one call per row. Each command is exactly what you would send to data_add_item / data_update_item / data_move_item / data_delete_item, as {type, ...args}: type is add_item | update_item | move_item | delete_item. All or nothing: the first failure rolls back everything and names which command failed. The reply is one line per command ({id, seq}) — not the rows, which you already have.

command_id.description: idempotency key — generate a fresh uuid per action

commands.description: [{type: "add_item", collection, fields, group?}, {type: "update_item", id, fields}, …] — same arguments as the single-write tools

name: data_batch

seq.description: the batch's last ledger position — pass it to data_changes as `since`

title: Many writes, one transaction

description: What happened in a collection after a ledger position YOU hold — including edits the USER made in the widget, which never pass through you. Any mark you already have works as `since`: a write ack's `seq`, data_list's `version`, or the last call's `next_since`. Returns the contiguous run of events right after it (oldest first, whole events: actor, item id, fields) plus `next_since` to continue; omit `since` to just learn the current position.

since.description: your held mark — events strictly after this seq; omit to just learn latest_seq

name: data_changes
title: What changed since you last looked

description: Count, sum, min, max or average a collection's items — optionally grouped by a field — WITHOUT the rows travelling anywhere. Use it for "how much did I spend per category", "how many are still open", "what is the largest": the answer comes back with `matched`, the number of rows it was computed over, so it can be checked. `match` takes exactly data_list's filter grammar. One collection, AND-ed filters, no joins — read the rows with data_list if you need something this cannot express.

group.description: restrict to one group/lane before aggregating

group_by.description: field to bucket by, e.g. "category" — biggest bucket first

match.description: same filter grammar as data_list's match

name: data_query

matched.description: rows the numbers were computed over — the audit trail of the answer

total.description: buckets that exist; if greater than returned, the smallest were omitted

title: Aggregate without reading the rows

description: The cheapest possible change check: returns the global change counter (seq) plus settings/files sub-counters. If seq hasn't moved since you last looked, NOTHING changed anywhere — skip re-reading. Widgets use this for adaptive polling; you can too before re-listing a collection.
name: data_version
title: Data change probe

description: List every data collection that exists (name, item count, last activity). Use when unsure where data lives, what boards the user has, or which collection to bind a component to. Renders no UI.
name: data_collections
title: List collections

description: Add an item to a collection. `group` is the component-defined lane/section (e.g. a kanban column); `fields` is a JSON object (e.g. {title, done, notes…}).

command_id.description: idempotency key — generate a fresh uuid per action

name: data_add_item
title: Add item

description: Shallow-merge fields into an item (set a key to null to remove it). Uses optimistic concurrency.

command_id.description: idempotency key — generate a fresh uuid per action

expected_version.description: the item version you last saw

name: data_update_item
title: Update item fields

description: Move an item to another group and/or position (e.g. kanban column).

command_id.description: idempotency key — generate a fresh uuid per action

name: data_move_item
title: Move item

description: Delete an item permanently.

command_id.description: idempotency key — generate a fresh uuid per action

name: data_delete_item
title: Delete item

description: List the files an app (component) has stored — a PAGE of {path, size, mime, version} plus usage totals; limit/cursor page through, prefix narrows. These are opaque user files (attachments, exports) the app keeps — separate from its structured data collection. Renders no UI.

component.description: the app whose files to list

cursor.description: opaque cursor from the previous page's next_cursor

prefix.description: only paths starting with this prefix

name: file_list
title: List app files

description: Read one file an app has stored, as a WINDOW of its bytes: offset/length select it, data_base64 carries exactly that window, next_offset continues (same window grammar as get_component, and for the same reason). Reassemble by concatenating decoded windows; sha256 is the WHOLE file's hash, so reassembly is checkable.

length.description: max bytes for this window (default fits the result budget)

name: file_read
title: Read an app file

description: Store a file for an app (create or overwrite by path). `data_base64` is the file bytes, base64-encoded — pass any file the user gave you or that you generated. Overwriting an existing path bumps its version. Single-call writes are limited to a few MiB. Files persist and are the app's own, reusable across chats.

command_id.description: idempotency key — a fresh uuid per write

component.description: the app this file belongs to

expected_version.description: the version you last saw, for optimistic concurrency (optional)

name: file_write
title: Store an app file

description: Start a chunked upload for a file too big for file_write's single call. Returns an upload_id; send the bytes in order with file_write_chunk (each chunk up to ~5 MiB of raw bytes), then file_write_commit names the file. Uploads expire after 30 idle minutes; per-file ceiling 250 MiB.

component.description: the app this file will belong to

name: file_write_begin
title: Begin a chunked file write

description: Append the next chunk of bytes (base64) to an upload started with file_write_begin. Send chunks strictly in order, one at a time. Pass `seq` (0-based chunk index) so a resend after a lost response is acknowledged instead of double-appended.

seq.description: 0-based index of this chunk — a resend of an already-staged index is a safe no-op

name: file_write_chunk
title: Append a chunk to an upload

description: Finalize an upload as an app file (create or overwrite by path) — the chunked equivalent of file_write. The upload is consumed either way; on failure, restart from file_write_begin.

command_id.description: idempotency key (uuid); auto-generated if omitted. A retried commit with the same id returns the original receipt instead of demanding a re-upload

expected_sha256.description: precheck: refuse (losslessly — the upload survives) if the staged bytes hash differently

name: file_write_commit
title: Commit a chunked file write

description: Discard an in-flight upload and its staged bytes. Safe to call on an already-gone upload.
name: file_write_abort
title: Abort a chunked file write

description: Permanently delete one file an app has stored.
name: file_delete
title: Delete an app file

description: List a component's saved versions as {version, ts, html_size} — metadata only, NEVER the html (keeps context small; use get_component for the current source). History survives delete_component (tombstone).
name: component_history
title: Component version history

description: Roll a component back to one of its earlier versions: re-saves that version's HTML as a NEW current version (nothing is lost — history is preserved and you can roll forward again). Use when a newer edit broke the UI. Find the version number with component_history; after restoring, open_component to view it.

version.description: the historical version to restore (see component_history)

name: restore_component
title: Restore a component version

description: Internal: the widget loader reports whether a component's html mounted cleanly. A failure report about the current version triggers an automatic rollback to the previous version (history preserved, max 3 per component per server run). Not normally called by the AI — use restore_component to roll back deliberately.

error.description: the uncaught error message, when ok=false

version.description: the component version that was rendering

name: render_health

new_version.description: the new current version number after the revert

restored_version.description: the historical version whose html is now current again

title: Report component render health (internal)

description: Remove a component from the registry permanently (confirm with the user first). Version history is RETAINED as a tombstone and its data collection / settings items are untouched. The component's ui:// registration may linger until server restart; open_component itself fails cleanly right away.

command_id.description: idempotency key — generate a fresh uuid per action

name: delete_component
title: Delete component

description: Browse the built-in library: ready-made, high-quality apps shipped with the engine that the user can install into their registry. Shows install state. Renders no UI — open_component {component: "library"} shows the browsable library app.
name: library_list

from_library.description: installed copy came from the library

title: List library apps

description: Internal: returns a library entry's html plus its embedded mock-data fixtures, so the library app can render a LIVE sandboxed preview card (srcdoc + stub oma + mock snapshot). Read-only; nothing is installed. Not useful to call directly.
name: library_preview

fixtures.description: embedded mock snapshot items, or null if the entry ships none

title: Library live-preview payload (internal)

description: Install (or update) a ready-made app from the built-in library into the user's registry. Once installed it behaves like any app of the user's own; its UI updates come from the library (newer library version), not from edits. Use library_list to see what's available. Installing is HALF the job: before handing it over, seed the collection with the user's real rows (data_batch, from what you already know of them) — an installed app opened empty and generic is half-delivered.
name: install_from_library
title: Install a library app

description: The engine-owned catalog of SHARED preferences (key, type, label, default, options) that the settings app renders. Components read effective values via oma.pref(); this tool only describes what exists. Read-only.
name: ui_prefs_schema
title: Shared preference catalog

description: For every component: its author, trust tier, whether it's a locked system component, and the effective capability grants (including file_read/file_write). This is what the settings Permissions pane renders. Read-only; capability OVERRIDES are written with security_set.
name: component_permissions
title: Component permissions overview

description: Privileged writer for reserved settings keys (security:* / policy:*) — the ONLY tool that can write them; the generic data_* tools refuse reserved keys. Upserts one key/value in the settings collection.

key.description: a reserved key, e.g. security:kanban:send_message (cap suffixes are snake_case — the caps field names)

value.description: the policy value, e.g. allow | ask | deny | confirm

name: security_set
title: Set a security policy key
